questions.question: What sum of money (in Rs) will produce Rs 75 as simple interest in 4 years at 1frac{1}2\% per annum?

Simple Interest (SI) = Rs 75

Time (T) = 4 years

Rate of Interest (R) = 1¹⁄₂% = 1.5%

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ⁄ 100

**Calculation:**

questions.question: 16 women can finish a task in 20 days and 20 men take 32 days to finish the same task. How many days will 8 women and 16 men take to finish the same task?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

16 women can finish a task in 20 days.

20 men can finish the same task in 32 days.

We need to find how many days 8 women and 16 men will take to finish the task.

**Formula Used:**

Work efficiency = Total work / Time taken

Total work is constant, and efficiency is directly proportional to the number of workers and inversely proportional to the time taken.

To solve combined work, we use the Least Common Multiple (LCM) method.

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM of (16 × 20, 20 × 32)

Total work = LCM(320, 640)

Total work = 640 units.

Work done by 16 women in 1 day = Total work / Days = 640 / 20 = 32 units/day.

Work done by 1 woman in 1 day = 32 / 16 = 2 units/day.

Work done by 20 men in 1 day = Total work / Days = 640 / 32 = 20 units/day.

Work done by 1 man in 1 day = 20 / 20 = 1 unit/day.

Work done by 8 women and 16 men in 1 day = (8 × 2) + (16 × 1)

Work done by 8 women and 16 men in 1 day = 16 + 16 = 32 units/day.

Time taken to complete the task = Total work / Work done per day.

⇒ Time = 640 / 32

⇒ Time = 20 days

**The time taken by 8 women and 16 men to complete the task is 20 days.**

questions.question: A solid sphere of radius 12 cm is melted and cast into small spherical balls, each of diameter 2.4 cm. Find the number of balls thus obtained.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the solid sphere = 12 cm.

Diameter of each small spherical ball = 2.4 cm.

Radius of each small spherical ball = Diameter / 2 = 2.4 / 2 = 1.2 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Number of small balls = Total volume of the solid sphere / Volume of one small ball

**Calculation:**

Volume of the solid sphere:

⇒ (4/3) × π × (12)³

⇒ (4/3) × π × 1728

⇒ 2304π cm³

Volume of one small ball:

⇒ (4/3) × π × (1.2)³

⇒ (4/3) × π × 1.728

⇒ 2.304π cm³

Number of small balls:

⇒ Total volume of the solid sphere / Volume of one small ball

⇒ 2304π / 2.304π

⇒ 1000

**The number of small balls obtained is 1000.**

questions.question: The circumference of the base of a cone is 66 cm and its height is 20 cm. Find the volume of the cone. (Use pi = frac{22}7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The circumference of the base of the cone = 66 cm.

Height of the cone = 20 cm.

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Where r is the radius, h is the height.

**Calculation:**

Circumference of the base = 2 × π × r

⇒ 66 = 2 × (22/7) × r

⇒ r = (66 × 7) / (2 × 22)

⇒ r = 21/2 cm

Volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (21/2)² × 20

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 441/4 × 20

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22 × 2205 / 7)

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22 × 315)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 105

⇒ Volume = 2310 cm³

**The volume of the cone is 2310 cm³.**

questions.question: The average of the first, second and third observations is 39, while the average of the second, third and fourth observations is 35. If the fourth observation is (3)/(5) times that of the first, then the value of the fourth observation is:

**Given:**

The average of the first, second, and third observations = 39

The average of the second, third, and fourth observations = 35

The fourth observation is (3/5) times the first observation.

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations / Number of observations

**Calculation:**

Let the first observation = A, second observation = B, third observation = C, fourth observation = D.

From the given data:

Sum of first, second, and third observations = 39 × 3 = 117

⇒ A + B + C = 117

Sum of second, third, and fourth observations = 35 × 3 = 105

⇒ B + C + D = 105

The fourth observation is (3/5) times the first observation:

⇒ D = (3/5) × A

Subtract the two equations:

(A + B + C) - (B + C + D) = 117 - 105

⇒ A - D = 12

Substitute D = (3/5) × A:

⇒ A - (3/5) × A = 12

⇒ (5A - 3A) / 5 = 12

⇒ 2A / 5 = 12

⇒ A = (12 × 5) / 2

⇒ A = 30

Now substitute A = 30 into D = (3/5) × A:

⇒ D = (3/5) × 30

⇒ D = 18

**The value of the fourth observation is 18.**

Profit Percentage = [(SP - CP) / CP] × 100

Marked price = Cost price + ₹37,000

Discount Price = Marked price × (1 - Discount%)

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be ₹x.

Marked price = x + ₹37,000

Discount price at 15% = (x + ₹37,000) × (1 - 15/100)

Discount price at 20% = (x + ₹37,000) × (1 - 20/100)

It is given that the 15% discount fetches ₹7,500 more than the 20% discount:

⇒ (x + ₹37,000) × (1 - 15/100) = (x + ₹37,000) × (1 - 20/100) + ₹7,500

⇒ (x + ₹37,000) × (85/100 - 80/100) = ₹7,500

⇒ (x + ₹37,000) × 5/100 = ₹7,500

⇒ x + ₹37,000 = ₹7,500 × 100 / 5

⇒ x + ₹37,000 = ₹1,50,000

⇒ x = ₹1,50,000 - ₹37,000

⇒ x = ₹1,13,000

**The cost price is ₹1,13,000.**

questions.question: A start from X at 9:00 A.M. and reaches Y at 1:00 P.M. on the same day, B also starts from Y at 9:00 A.M. and reaches X at 3:00 P.M. on the same day, following the same route as A. At what time do the two meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A starts from X at 9:00 A.M. and reaches Y at 1:00 P.M. (time taken = 4 hours).

B starts from Y at 9:00 A.M. and reaches X at 3:00 P.M. (time taken = 6 hours).

The distance between X and Y is the same for both A and B.

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Speed of A + Speed of B

Distance = Speed × Time

Meeting time = Distance covered by A or B till meeting point / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between X and Y = D.

Speed of A = D / 4.

Speed of B = D / 6.

Relative Speed = (D / 4) + (D / 6).

⇒ Relative Speed = (3D + 2D) / 12 = 5D / 12.

Both start at 9:00 A.M., so let the time taken to meet = t hours.

Distance covered by A till meeting point = Distance covered by B till meeting point.

Distance covered by A = Speed of A × t = (D / 4) × t.

Distance covered by B = Speed of B × t = (D / 6) × t.

Total distance covered by A and B together = D.

⇒ (D / 4) × t + (D / 6) × t = D.

Take LCM of 4 and 6, which is 12:

⇒ (3D / 12) × t + (2D / 12) × t = D.

⇒ (5D / 12) × t = D.

⇒ t = 12 / 5 = 2.4 hours.

Convert 2.4 hours to hours and minutes: 2 hours and 24 minutes.

Meeting time = 9:00 A.M. + 2 hours 24 minutes = 11:24 A.M.

**The two meet at 11:24 A.M.**

questions.question:
If a reduction of 10% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 22 kg more for ₹250, then the original price of the rice per kg is:

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Reduction in price = 10%.

Amount spent = ₹250.

Extra rice obtained = 22 kg.

**Formula Used:**

Original price per kg = (Reduction Amount × 100) / (Reduction Percentage × Extra Quantity).

**Calculation:**

Let the original price of rice per kg be ₹x.

Reduced price per kg = ₹(x - 10% of x) = ₹(0.9x).

Quantity of rice bought at original price = ₹250 / x.

Quantity of rice bought at reduced price = ₹250 / (0.9x).

Given, the difference in quantity is 22 kg:

⇒ ₹250 / (0.9x) - ₹250 / x = 22.

⇒ 250(1 / 0.9x - 1 / x) = 22.

⇒ 250((x - 0.9x) / (0.9x × x)) = 22.

⇒ 250(0.1x / 0.9x²) = 22.

⇒ (250 × 0.1) / (0.9x) = 22.

⇒ 25 / (0.9x) = 22.

⇒ 25 = 22 × 0.9x.

⇒ 25 = 19.8x.

⇒ x = 25 / 19.8.

⇒ x = 1.26.

**The original price of rice per kg is ₹1.26.**

questions.question: Which element is located in Group 18 of the periodic table and is known for its lack of chemical reactivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Helium** is a chemical element and is part of **Group 18** (Noble Gases) in the **Periodic Table**.
 
• It is known for its **inertness** due to its full valence electron shell, making it highly stable and almost non-reactive under normal conditions.
 
• **Helium** has **two protons** and is represented by the symbol **He**.
 
• It is the **second-lightest** and **second-most abundant element** in the universe, following hydrogen.
 
• Helium is a **colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas** at room temperature and is widely used for applications requiring non-reactivity, such as in balloons, cryogenics, and as a protective gas in welding.
 
• Its **low boiling point** (-268.93°C) makes it useful in applications like cooling superconducting magnets in MRI machines.
 
• As a noble gas, helium has **no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons**, which explains its lack of chemical reactivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Oxygen**__

 __
 
• **Oxygen** is a highly reactive element and belongs to **Group 16** of the periodic table, also known as the chalcogens.
 
• It is essential for **respiration** in living organisms and is a part of the Earth's atmosphere (~21%).
 
• Oxygen readily forms compounds, such as water (H₂O), due to its high electronegativity.
 
• It is not inert and reacts with many elements and compounds.
 
 
 
• ** Chlorine**__
 __
 
• **Chlorine** is a highly reactive halogen belonging to **Group 17** of the periodic table.
 
• It is widely used as a **disinfectant** and in the production of **plastics** like PVC (polyvinyl chloride).
 
• Chlorine forms compounds such as sodium chloride (common salt) and is not chemically inert.
 
 
 
• ** Fluorine**__
 
 
• **Fluorine** is the most reactive element in the periodic table and belongs to **Group 17** (halogens).
 
• It has a high electronegativity, which makes it highly reactive with most elements, including some noble gases under specific conditions.
 
• Fluorine compounds, such as fluoride, are widely used in toothpaste and water fluoridation to prevent dental cavities.

• One-twelfth are elected by graduates residing in the state.
 
• One-twelfth are elected by teachers in the state who have been teaching for at least three years.
 
• One-sixth are **nominated by the Governor** of the state from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, cooperative movement, or social service.
 
 
 
• The Legislative Council acts as a **reviewing chamber** and is intended to provide a check on hasty legislation passed by the Legislative Assembly.
 
• Not all states in India have a Legislative Council. Currently, only a few states, such as **Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana**, have bicameral legislatures.
 
• The Legislative Council’s existence and composition are governed by the provisions laid out in **Article 171**.

• **Article 169**__
